Article Title: Ex-top Chhattisgarh official behind paper leaks, appointed kin as deputy collector, DSP: ED
Article Text:
Representative image

ED has taken custodial remand of Taman Singh Sonwani, a retired IAS who served as chairperson of Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission (CGPSC), in an alleged case of paper leak and manipulation of CGPSC state service exam.Sonwani in 2021 allegedly amended recruitment rules of CGPSC to remove "nephew" from the definition of "family" and appointed his family members as deputy collector and DSP, according to ED.A special court in Raipur has remanded him to ED custody for seven days, till July 30 for further investigation. The former IAS officer was arrested on July 25.
Article Summary: Taman Singh Sonwani was chairperson of Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission. He allegedly amended recruitment rules of CGPSC to remove "nephew" from definition of "family" and appointed his family members as deputy collector and DSP. He was arrested on July 25.

Article Title: 'Modi govt fears truth and non-violence': Rahul Gandhi on Ken-Betwa protest crackdown
Article Text:
Police cleared the protest site on July 19

Rahul Gandhi X post

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday said the Narendra Modi government fears "both truth and non-violent resistance", days after police dispersed tribal protests against the Ken-Betwa river linking project in BJP-led Madhya Pradesh."The tribal brothers and sisters of Madhya Pradesh had sat on a water satyagraha and hunger strike because their land was taken away for the Ken-Betwa project, but they received neither fair compensation nor dignified rehabilitation," the Lok Sabha leader of opposition wrote on X.Calling tribals the country's "original owners", Rahul Gandhi asserted that the first right over water, forests and land "belongs to them alone.""And their 'satyagraha' is because that very right is being snatched from them today. In their unique way, their demand is simply this: provide a proper means of livelihood—or else life is no different from a funeral pyre. But even this is unacceptable to the BJP government. Instead of listening to them, their peaceful protest is being crushed with police force," the Raebareli MP added.The former Congress chief expressed solidarity with the protesting tribal communities and asserted that his party would ensure justice, including fair compensation and proper rehabilitation for them.Rahul Gandhi also shared a video clip highlighting the protests in Madhya Pradesh.On July 19, police in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district removed protesters from the site, bringing their 15-day agitation to an end.The Rs 44,605-crore Ken-Betwa Link Project is India's first river-linking project under the National Perspective Plan. It aims to irrigate 1.062 million hectares of land, provide drinking water to around 6.2 million people, and generate hydropower in the drought-prone Bundelkhand region spanning Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi: Narendra Modi government fears "both truth and non-violent resistance" Police dispersed tribal protests against the Ken-Betwa river linking project in Madhya Pradesh. The Rs 44,605-crore project is India's first river- linking project under the National Perspective Plan.

Article Title: NEET fast-track court's first hearing stalls as CBI skips proceedings
Article Text:
NEET fast-track court's first hearing stalled as CBI skips proceedings

NEW DELHI: The first hearing before Delhi's newly designated fast-track court for the NEET paper leak case ended without any substantive proceedings on Monday after no lawyer appeared on behalf of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), prompting the court to adjourn the matter.The case came up before Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga, who recently assumed charge of the special court set up to exclusively hear offences related to paper leaks and other unfair means in public examinations.The court was scheduled to hear the bail applications of two accused, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal. However, with no prosecutor representing the investigating agency present until 10.45 am, the judge recorded the absence in the order, news agency PTI reported.Counsel for the accused requested that the matter be deferred, informing the court that he had to appear in another case before the Rohini district courts and could not wait further. Accepting the request, the judge adjourned the hearing to August 3.The court also directed the director of prosecution to ensure that a public prosecutor is deputed to the designated court for the next hearing.The fast-track court began functioning on Saturday after the Delhi high court notified it as a specially designated court to try offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, along with related criminal cases.The notification followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement that dedicated fast-track courts would be established to expedite trials in paper leak cases.The NEET paper leak case was previously being heard by Special Judge Ajay Gupta. On Friday, he extended the judicial custody of all 13 accused until August 6 and rejected the bail plea of paediatrician Dr Manoj Bhagwanrao Shirure. In its order, the court observed that the investigation prima facie indicated Shirure was "one of the active conspirators of an organised paper leak gang."The controversy erupted after allegations of irregularities in the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate) conducted on May 3. Following widespread protests, the National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the examination on May 12 and conducted a re-test on June 21.
Article Summary: The first hearing before Delhi's newly designated fast-track court for the NEET paper leak case ended without any substantive proceedings on Monday. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the Central Bureau of Investigation, prompting the court to adjourn the matter. The controversy erupted after allegations of irregularities in the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate) conducted on May 3.

Article Title: IRB constable on Wari duty ends life by suicide
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A 30-year-old armed police constable of the Indian Reserve Battalion (IRB) in Kolhapur shot himself from his service rifle at a makeshift shelter at Kasegaon near Pandharpur early on Saturday.The deceased, Rameshwar Dhrupad Sabane, was a native of Gangakhed in Parbhani district. He was deployed on duty for Ashadi Ekadashi for the last three weeks. After returning from duty around 2.30am on Saturday he shot himself and took his life, while the rest of his mates were asleep.Sabane was rushed to Pandharpur for treatment. However, the doctors declared him dead. The motive behind taking the extreme step by Sabane is not yet clear, but preliminary investigation has found that he had personal issues and was distressed because he was unable to get leave to address the issue.A case of suicide has been registered at Pandharpur rural police station.
Article Summary: The deceased, Rameshwar Dhrupad Sabane, was a native of Gangakhed in Parbhani district. He was deployed on duty for Ashadi Ekadashi for the last three weeks. The motive behind taking the extreme step by Sabane is not yet clear, but preliminary investigation has found that he had personal issues.

Article Title: Congress stages rasta roko in Kalyan over police action on Jantar Mantar protesters
Article Text:
Congress workers staged a protest in Kalyan West against alleged police action.





KALYAN: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West to protest against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi over the alleged paper leak issue.Led by Navin Singh, Kalyan District President, the protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators by the Delhi Police.Traffic was briefly affected in the area before police intervened.The party also submitted a memorandum to the Kalyan tehsildar, addressed to the President of India, seeking an inquiry into the alleged police action against students and Congress leaders, including Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other party leaders, during the protest at Delhi.In the memorandum, the Congress demanded the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, holding him morally responsible for the alleged irregularities in the paper leak. The party also sought an urgent discussion in Parliament on alleged examination irregularities and issues affecting students' future.The memorandum further demanded that all FIRs and criminal cases registered against students and peaceful protesters be withdrawn immediately.Among those present at the protest were corporator Samina Sheikh, former corporator Iftekar Khan and other Congress office-bearers and workers. Police maintained security at the protest site and ensured traffic movement was restored after the demonstration concluded.
Article Summary: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West. They were protesting against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar violence echoes in KDMC house meet as opposition, MNS protest police action
Article Text:
As soon as the proceedings began, opposition members stood up, shouted slogans and disrupted the House.





KALYAN: The Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC) General Body meeting on Thursday witnessed high drama as opposition corporators staged a protest against the alleged police action against students demonstrating at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Corporators from the opposition, including the Shiv Sena (UBT), Congress and NCP (SP), entered the House carrying the Tricolour and wearing black armbands as a mark of protest. Raising slogans of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram", they demanded that the House be adjourned to condemn the police action and express solidarity with the injured protesters.As soon as the proceedings began, opposition members stood up, shouted slogans and disrupted the House, forcing Mayor Harshali Chaudhary to adjourn the meeting for 10 minutes.However, after the House reconvened, the opposition continued its protest, condemning what it termed police brutality at Jantar Mantar and urging corporators from the ruling alliance to join them.The protest also witnessed an unusual political alignment, with the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), a ruling ally of the Shiv Sena in the KDMC, joining hands with the Shiv Sena (UBT) during the demonstration. The BJP took a swipe at the MNS, saying that if MNS corporators wished to sit with the opposition, they should first resign from the ruling alliance and formally move to the opposition benches.Differences within the ruling alliance also came to the fore during the debate. Shiv Sena corporator Mahesh Gaikwad demanded that the House observe a two-minute silence in memory of the students who were allegedly injured in the police action. BJP group leader Shashikant Kamble objected, stating that several police personnel were also injured during the Jantar Mantar protest and that, if a condolence gesture was to be made, it should include them as well.Despite the noisy scenes and repeated slogan-shouting, the General Body meeting continued. Later, leaders of the Shiv Sena and BJP jointly cleared several civic proposals without detailed discussion, while a few agenda items were deferred for consideration at a later meeting.
Article Summary: Corporators from the opposition, including the Shiv Sena (UBT), Congress and NCP (SP), entered the House carrying the Tricolour and wearing black armbands as a mark of protest. Raising slogans of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram", they demanded that the House be adjourned.

Article Title: Three arrested for supplying ganja to techies, students in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: The Prohibition Enforcement Wing (PEW) of the Coimbatore city police on Saturday arrested three men for supplying ganja to IT professionals and students here.The arrested have been identified as A Gowtham, 25, of Ganapathy, A Rahul Kumar of Avarampalayam and S Dinesh Kumar, 26, of Kurumapalayam.Acting on specific intelligence about individuals involved in ganja supply to IT professionals and students in the Saravanampatti and Kalapatti neighbourhoods, PEW police led by inspector M Miadit Mano conducted a check near Sungam. They intercepted a car and found ganja in it.Following this, police seized the car and took the trio to the police station for further inquiry, which revealed that they used two more cars and a motorcycle to supply ganja. Police seized three cars, a motorcycle and 4 kg of ganja from them.Police registered a case against them under sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. The trio were remanded in judicial custody. Police have initiated a process to freeze their bank accounts.
Article Summary: The Prohibition Enforcement Wing (PEW) of the Coimbatore city police on Saturday arrested three men for supplying ganja to IT professionals and students. The arrested have been identified as A Gowtham, 25, of Ganapathy, A Rahul Kumar of Avarampalayam and S Dinesh Kumar, 26. Police have initiated a process to freeze their bank accounts.

Article Title: Sengottaiyan flays previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies on Mekedatu dam issue
Article Text:
K A Sengottaiyan





ERODE: Tamil Nadu revenue minister K A Sengottaiyan on Saturday criticized the previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies to stop Karnataka’s move to build a dam across the Cauvery river in Mekedatu.Speaking at a consultation meeting of officials from different departments held at the Erode district collectorate, Sengottaiyan reiterated that chief minister C Joseph Vijay had urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to halt the move to build a dam in Mekedatu.During the review meeting, the minister told officials to deliver results quickly, saying the govt’s performance since coming to power warranted a thorough review and that the people’s demands should be met without delay. “Officers must complete necessary office procedures promptly and ensure citizens receive timely relief,” he told reporters after the meeting.The review, chaired by district collector S Kandasamy and also attended by handloom minister M Vijay Balaji, covered a wide range of administrative concerns.A major focus was the Athikadavu-Avinashi integrated drinking water project. Officials were directed to find out why more than 70 ponds were not getting filled and asked them to take remedial measures. Officials were instructed to begin silt-removal operations in the Bhavanisagar Dam to improve storage capacity and downstream supply.On allegations that liquor outlets were operating in violation of regulations, the revenue minister demanded concrete statistics and warned that strict action would follow where breaches were confirmed.
Article Summary: K A Sengottaiyan criticized the previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies to stop Karnataka’s move to build a dam across the Cauvery river in Mekedatu. He reiterated that chief minister C Joseph Vijay had urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to halt the move.

Article Title: Teen held after 2 schoolboys found dead in well
Article Text:
19-year-old boy on Sunday on charges of murdering two school-going brothers





Theni: Police arrested a 19-year-old boy on Sunday on charges of murdering two school-going brothers by pushing them into a deep well near Bodinayakkanur in Theni district.Police identified the deceased as Sriharis, 11, and Sabareesh, 10, sons of Chinnathambi and Selvi of Renganathapuram near Bodinayakkanur. They were studying in Class VI and V respectively at a govt-aided middle school in the locality.According to Bodinayakkanur rural police, the brothers went missing on Friday evening after school. Based on a complaint filed by their parents, police registered a case and launched a search operation.During the investigation, police examined CCTV footage from a nearby temple where the boys were seen along with Kesava Balaji, 19, a college dropout from the area.They bought and consumed porridge (koozh).When police questioned Balaji, he gave contradictory statements, raising suspicion. Further interrogation revealed that he took the boys to a coconut grove near Muneeswaran Odai at Karattupatti and pushed them into the 150-foot-well.On Saturday evening, fire and rescue personnel retrieved the two bodies, which were sent to Theni Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem.Balaji was arrested on Sunday and remanded in judicial custody. Police are trying to ascertain the motive behind the crime.
Article Summary: Police identified the deceased as Sriharis, 11, and Sabareesh, 10, sons of Chinnathambi and Selvi of Renganathapuram near Bodinayakkanur. They were studying in Class VI and V respectively at a govt-aided middle school.

Article Text:
Actor Ansiba Hassan

Kochi

:





Ernakulam judicial first class magistrate court dismissed a petition filed by actor Ansiba Hassan seeking directions for registering an FIR on her complaint against actor Lakshmipriya and two persons connected to an online media outlet.Ansiba approached the court, accusing them of circulating videos on social media to tarnish her image and subjecting her to public humiliation. The court examined the complaint, supporting affidavit and the submission made by the Palarivattom SHO before finding that there was no cognisable offence presently made out that can be forwarded to the SHO.After Ansiba approached the court alleging police inaction, the court directed the police to submit an explanation on July 9.Palarivattom SHO submitted that a preliminary inquiry was conducted after securing permission from the Ernakulam assistant commissioner. Six persons were questioned, their statements recorded and the concerned videos were collected from the YouTube channel. As per the SHO, there was no scope for invoking cognisable offences, and the matter attracted only BNS Section 356 (criminal defamation).
Article Summary: Ansiba Hassan accused Lakshmipriya and two persons connected to an online media outlet of circulating videos on social media to tarnish her image. Ernakulam judicial first class magistrate court dismissed a petition filed by actor Ansiba Hassan seeking directions for registering an FIR.
